agents.name: Osimertinib

sections.title: Supplies and visits
sections.text: Arrange repeat prescriptions before tablets run out. Keep blood and ECG appointments. The oral regimen does not itself need an infusion line or pump.

sections.title: If treatment is held
sections.text: Ask why it is held, what must recover, when review is due and who will authorise restarting. Do not choose between 80 mg and 40 mg yourself.

sections.title: At completion or change
sections.text: Agree scans, symptom follow-up, the medicine plan and contraception after the final dose.

evidence.title: Evidence depends on the treatment setting
evidence.intro: Adjuvant and advanced trials answer different questions.
evidence.population: Resected Ex19del/L858R disease; untreated advanced Ex19del/L858R disease; or advanced T790M disease after an earlier EGFR inhibitor.
evidence.interpretation: The evidence differs by setting. In a study after complete surgery, adjuvant osimertinib improved survival compared with placebo. In untreated advanced EGFR-mutated cancer, it improved survival compared with older EGFR tablets. After resistance with T790M, it delayed progression compared with platinum/pemetrexed, but the final overall-survival comparison was not statistically significant. These results describe selected study groups and cannot predict your own outcome.
evidence.limitations: Study averages cannot give an individual prognosis or compare today’s treatment options head to head. Chemotherapy-combination and post-chemoradiation studies require a separate discussion.

patient.teachback: Can you explain your treatment aim and duration, how you take the tablet, which heart/blood tests are next, and which symptoms mean you should call today?
patient.consent_support: Discuss adjuvant versus advanced intent, expected benefit and uncertainty, alternatives including not proceeding, common skin/bowel effects, serious lung/heart/skin/blood problems, fertility and pregnancy, daily tablets, monitoring and your right to reconsider.

support.title: Skin and nails
support.text: Agree an EGFR-inhibitor skin-care plan from the start and report rash or painful nail changes early. Blistering, peeling or mucosal sores need urgent assessment.

support.title: Bowel symptoms and hydration
support.text: Report diarrhoea early, follow the prescribed symptom plan and maintain fluids if able. Severe diarrhoea, weakness or reduced urine needs urgent advice.

support.title: Nausea medicines
support.text: Osimertinib has minimal-to-low oral emetic risk. Routine infusion premedication is not usually needed. Agree rescue medicines individually, including QT and interaction review; do not copy a chemotherapy antiemetic course.

support.title: Medicine interactions
support.text: Tell the team about all medicines and supplements. Do not take St John’s wort. Strong enzyme-inducing medicines and medicines that affect heart rhythm require pharmacy review before changes.

support.title: Pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding
support.text: Avoid pregnancy during treatment. Effective contraception continues for at least two months after the final dose for women and four months for men. Osimertinib may reduce hormonal contraceptive effectiveness; discuss a suitable method. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Discuss fertility and plans for pregnancy before starting.

key_points: NCCP00353a T790M advanced, b first-line activating-EGFR advanced and c adjuvant Ex19del/L858R IB–IIIA are distinct.
Daily oral monotherapy without a rest week; adjuvant three-year studied limit differs from advanced continuous duration.
Suspected ILD interrupts; confirmed ILD permanently stops under NCCP regardless of grade.
QTc >500 ms on two ECGs: hold to source recovery criterion then 40 mg; serious arrhythmia with prolongation permanently stops.
Severe hepatic and renal/dialysis source conflicts need Consultant/pharmacy review without automatic dose calculation.
NCCP CTCAE v4.0 retained; current EMA table uses v5.0.

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Adjuvant recurrence-risk reduction or advanced disease control; select the exact indication.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Adults with locally advanced or metastatic EGFR T790M mutation-positive NSCLC.
First-line treatment of adults with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with activating EGFR mutations.
Adjuvant monotherapy after complete resection of stage IB–IIIA NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R substitution.
eligibility_orientation: NCCP00353a/b/c indication-specific molecular and stage criteria; validated EGFR testing.
Adjuvant start within 10 weeks of resection without chemotherapy; if chemotherapy used, complete at most four platinum-doublet cycles and start 2–10 weeks after final dose.
important_cautions: Hypersensitivity, congenital long QT syndrome, pregnancy or breastfeeding.
For adjuvant: neoadjuvant/adjuvant radiation, neoadjuvant chemotherapy or prior EGFR inhibitor therapy.

ADAURA randomised completely resected stage IB–IIIA Ex19del/L858R disease, with or without prior adjuvant chemotherapy; survival runs from randomisation, not surgery or diagnosis. Stage II–IIIA and overall IB–IIIA results are separate.

FLAURA enrolled untreated advanced Ex19del/L858R NSCLC and compared older EGFR TKIs; it does not establish outcomes for every uncommon activating mutation or superiority over contemporary combination options.

AURA3 enrolled T790M-positive disease progressing after an earlier EGFR TKI. Its PFS benefit is not an OS benefit; extensive crossover affects OS interpretation. It is not a trial of treatment after first-line osimertinib.
LAURA post-chemoradiation and FLAURA2 combination populations are separate from the three NCCP00353 v5 indications; their outcomes are not assigned to this monotherapy suite.
Previous ILD, drug-induced ILD, steroid-treated radiation pneumonitis or active ILD were clinical-study exclusions; assess before treatment.
Baseline QTc >470 ms was a trial exclusion; congenital long QT is a separate NCCP exclusion.
Consider baseline and ongoing LVEF assessment with cardiac risk factors, relevant conditions or symptoms.
NCCP advises closer monitoring for age >65 years or body weight <50 kg; EMA does not require dose adjustment solely for age or weight.

These results describe selected study groups and cannot predict your own outcome.

endpoints.metric: ADAURA: five-year OS, overall stage IB–IIIA
endpoints.interpretation: 682 patients after complete resection; secondary OS endpoint; five years from randomisation, not surgery.
Stage II–IIIA analysis; 21% death-event maturity. Do not interchange with the overall IB–IIIA estimate.

endpoints.metric: FLAURA: median OS in untreated advanced disease
endpoints.interpretation: 556 untreated advanced Ex19del/L858R patients; secondary final OS endpoint; P=0.046. Older EGFR-TKI comparator, not a contemporary chemotherapy-combination comparison.
419 T790M-positive advanced NSCLC patients after progression on first-line EGFR TKI; time to progression or death from randomisation.
Same 419-patient trial; OS difference not statistically significant (P=0.277). High crossover (73% of treated comparator patients) complicates interpretation; no proven OS advantage.

selector.scope_note: This guide covers NCCP00353 osimertinib on its own: T790M-positive advanced disease, first-line activating-EGFR advanced disease, or completely resected stage IB–IIIA Ex19del/L858R adjuvant treatment. The newer licensed post-chemoradiation setting and osimertinib with platinum/pemetrexed need their own applicable plan; their study results and support medicines are not added to this monotherapy suite.

support_plans.label: Osimertinib alone · daily oral treatment
additional_support: Agree an EGFR-inhibitor skin-care plan from the start and report rash or painful nail changes early. Blistering, peeling or mucosal sores need urgent assessment.
Report diarrhoea early, follow the prescribed symptom plan and maintain fluids if able. Severe diarrhoea, weakness or reduced urine needs urgent advice.

Osimertinib has minimal-to-low oral emetic risk. Routine infusion premedication is not usually needed. Agree rescue medicines individually, including QT and interaction review; do not copy a chemotherapy antiemetic course.
Tell the team about all medicines and supplements. Do not take St John’s wort. Strong enzyme-inducing medicines and medicines that affect heart rhythm require pharmacy review before changes.

Avoid pregnancy during treatment. Effective contraception continues for at least two months after the final dose for women and four months for men. Osimertinib may reduce hormonal contraceptive effectiveness; discuss a suitable method. Do not breastfeed during treatment. Discuss fertility and plans for pregnancy before starting.
NCCP V6 Table 5 supports as-required oral antiemetics for minimal-low risk; select the agent, dose and duration individually after QT, renal and interaction review.

guidance.label: NCCP V6 Table 5: minimal-low oral therapy uses as-required antiemetics; NCIS V8 is parenteral and does not establish a mandatory oral prescription

risk.mapping_basis: NCCP00353 v5 minimal-to-low; individual oral rescue support, with QT/interaction review. NCIS V8 parenteral rows are not copied.
